world.h: Allies and UN back ICC against new US sanctions
world.b: European states, Canada, Japan and the UN condemned new US sanctions on the International Criminal Court after Secretary of State Marco Rubio banned transactions with the court.
world.title: European states, Canada, Japan and UN back ICC against US sanctions

world.b: Russian diesel is set to hit global markets as Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump discussed Iran, Al Jazeera reports.
world.title: Iran war updates: Saudi-led coalition hits Houthis; Putin, Trump talk Iran

world.h: Ukraine pushes Russia back in Donetsk
world.b: Russian forces continue to retreat in Ukraine's Donetsk region, losing villages south of Lyman, a Kremlin-aligned channel said.

world.h: Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize
world.b: South African jurist Navi Pillay, who led the UN inquiry that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza, won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.
more: She was UN high commissioner for human rights from 2008 to 2014 and president of the Rwanda war crimes tribunal.
world.title: Navi Pillay, South African Jurist, Wins Nobel Peace Prize in “Stinging Rebuke to Donald Trump”

national.h: Trump says U.S. will get diesel from Russia
national.b: President Trump said he struck a deal with Vladimir Putin for Russian diesel, reversing years of U.S. pressure on Moscow as fuel prices stay high before the midterms.
more: Trump said Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, with an additional 500,000 tons in November.
national.title: Trump says U.S. to get diesel from Russia, relaxing pressure on Moscow to ease prices before midterms

national.h: Narrow legal path to stop execution livestream
national.b: Experts say any challenge to the plan to livestream the firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan may rest with Hasan alone.
more: Hasan, sentenced to death for killing 13 people at the Texas base in 2009, has not said whether he will try to stop anything related to his Dec. 3 execution.
national.title: Legal path seems narrow to challenge livestream of Fort Hood shooter's execution, experts say

national.h: Pentagon gave firm tied to official $281M deal
national.b: ProPublica reports the Pentagon signed a no-bid $281 million consulting contract with a firm tied to senior defense official George Kollitides.
national.title: The Pentagon Gave $350 Million in Contracts to a Firm Closely Tied to a Senior Defense Department Official

national.h: NY proposes tighter sports betting rules
national.b: New York gambling regulators formally proposed two rules aimed at curbing gambling addiction in the country's largest sports betting market.
national.title: New York Plans Stronger Sports Betting Regulation to Curb Gambling Addiction

national.h: ICE says officers feared for lives in NYC shooting
national.b: A senior ICE official said officers shot Oscar Belgal, 28, in New York after he drove his car into their vehicles; he was shot superficially in the neck.

national.h: Arlington County sues over Trump's arch
national.b: Virginia's Arlington County Board sued to oppose Trump's planned Triumphal Arch at Memorial Circle, the first government body to do so.
more: The suit says the project skipped the full review process.

national.h: Plague still found in US and Africa yearly
national.b: The plague never went away: the US averages about seven human cases a year, mostly in the rural West, the CDC says. It is now easily treated with antibiotics.

national.h: Paxton's travel security cost Texas millions
national.b: ProPublica reports Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton's taxpayer-funded security detail on his travels cost millions.
more: While suspended in 2023 awaiting his impeachment trial, he took at least 17 trips, including to Park City, Utah, and Vail, Colorado.
national.title: Ken Paxton’s Security for Travel Cost Taxpayers Millions. Just 1 in 6 of His Trips Had a Stated Business Purpose.

national.h: Maricopa housing hub fails homeless families
national.b: A ProPublica investigation found Maricopa County's Family Housing Hub has become a dead end for many homeless families.
more: A 2023 evaluation found 94% of people assessed for housing help through the system did not receive it.
national.title: An Arizona County’s “Housing Hub” Is a Dead End for Many Homeless Families

national.h: Mamdani: ICE agent shot man in car with child
national.b: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said an ICE agent shot a man in Marble Hill after agents surrounded him and a five-year-old child in his car, calling it "unconscionable."

politics.h: Katie Zacharia picked as White House press secretary
politics.b: President Trump confirmed conservative commentator Katie Zacharia as his next press secretary.
politics.title: Katie Zacharia selected to be next White House press secretary

politics.h: Trump forms panel to probe Fed's Lisa Cook
politics.b: President Trump set up a "committee of inquiry" into mortgage allegations against Fed Governor Lisa Cook, with a private White House hearing Nov. 5.
politics.title: Trump establishes committee to investigate Federal Reserve's Lisa Cook in latest effort to fire her

politics.h: El-Sayed, Rogers meet in Michigan Senate debate
politics.b: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers faced off in their first televised debate in Michigan's toss-up Senate race.

international.h: 7.7 quake hits Panama, tsunami warnings issued
international.b: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama, prompting tsunami warnings for Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Nicaragua and Guatemala, and from Chile.
international.title: Tsunami warnings across Latin America after 7.7 magnitude earthquake hits

international.h: UN envoy: Yemen back in 'full-scale war'
international.b: UN envoy Hans Grundberg told the Security Council that Yemen has slid back into full-scale war, with civilians bearing the brunt, and urged dialogue.
international.title: UN envoy warns Yemen has returned to ‘full-scale war’, urges dialogue

international.h: UAE: Flydubai co-pilot plotted attack on Israel
international.b: Emirati authorities say the co-pilot who tried to seize a Flydubai plane on Sept. 30 meant to crash it at Israel's Ben Gurion airport.
international.title: Flydubai co-pilot plotted ‘suicide’ attack on Israel, UAE says

international.b: Ethiopia accused Eritrea of an "all-out invasion" in a letter to the UN Security Council, while Eritrea says it faces a "war of aggression."
Thousands rallied in Brussels against the government's austerity plans, and a smaller group clashed with police near Central station.
Ethiopian federal forces entered Mekelle after nearly two weeks of fighting, as rebel forces including the TPLF withdrew.
more: The fighting has effectively ended the 2022 Pretoria ceasefire.
There are reports of Eritrean troops entering northern Tigrayan towns.

international.h: UN concerned over French student protests
international.b: The UN voiced concern over sometimes violent clashes with police as French students plan more protests demanding better schools.
The UN Security Council extended the Darfur arms embargo until December 11 but did not agree to a US plan to widen it to all of Sudan, after Russia and China objected.

international.h: Police probe Sinn Fein over parade protest
international.b: Northern Ireland police contacted Sinn Fein representatives in an investigation into a protest that blocked a Protestant parade through a Catholic area, the party said.
more: The DUP, which shares power with Sinn Fein, has called for its lawmakers to be prosecuted.

business.h: Fuel costs cut Delta profit outlook
business.b: Atlanta-based Delta Air Lines lowered its profit forecast despite strong demand, saying it expects annual fuel costs to jump by $6 billion.
business.title: Rising fuel costs slashed Delta’s profit outlook despite strong demand

business.h: Fired OpenAI workers question safety commitment
business.b: Three former OpenAI employees allege they were fired for being outspoken about safety. OpenAI disputes that and says they mishandled sensitive information.
business.title: Fired OpenAI employees question the company's commitment to safety

business.b: The Gulf Coast oil industry began preparing days ago for Hurricane Isaias, expected to make landfall Friday evening near the Alabama coast and Florida Panhandle.

The Trump administration barred Microsoft, Adobe and a handful of other companies from sponsoring foreign workers for green cards for now, and proposed a big fee increase for students' OPT work visas.
more: It also announced an investigation into nine universities over the J-1 student visa program.
business.title: International students could see a massive fee increase for OPT work visa

sports.h: Valkyries sweep Aces to reach WNBA Finals
sports.b: The second-year Golden State Valkyries beat the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces 87-77 in overtime to finish a semifinal sweep and reach their first WNBA Finals.
sports.title: Golden State Valkyries reach WNBA Finals: How second-year franchise made unprecedented run

sports.b: Mike Ditka, the Hall of Fame tight end who coached the Bears to their only Super Bowl title, has died at 86, his family said.

local.h: DSA urges Mamdani to fire NYPD commissioner
local.b: The city's Democratic Socialists of America chapter is pressuring Mayor Zohran Mamdani to fire his police commissioner if ICE doesn't leave New York City.
local.title: DSA to Mamdani: Fire NYPD commissioner if ICE doesn't leave NYC

local.h: Two killed in Bronx vehicle crash
local.b: Two people died and several were injured when a car rear-ended four vehicles on Allerton Avenue in the Bronx on Friday, police said.
local.title: Two people killed in Bronx vehicle crash

local.h: NY will opt in to Trump school choice program
local.b: Gov. Kathy Hochul said New York will join the Trump administration's school choice program despite teachers unions' fears it will divert money from public schools.
local.title: NY will opt in Trump’s school choice program, Hochul says

local.h: DA fights dismissal of Mangione charges
local.b: The Manhattan DA argued a judge should not dismiss state charges against Luigi Mangione.
local.title: Manhattan DA argues judge shouldn't dismiss state charges against Luigi Mangione

local.h: Judge: ICE lied after mistaken Bronx arrests
local.b: A federal judge ruled ICE agents mistakenly arrested two men in the Bronx and then lied in sworn testimony to cover it up.
local.title: ICE mistakenly arrested 2 men in the Bronx, then mounted cover-up, US judge rules

local.b: City Council members are calling on education officials to let students return to paper tests as the state mandates screens.
local.title: Pencils down: NYC lawmakers want to switch back to paper tests as state mandates screens

local.h: Five arrested at ICE shooting protest
local.b: Police said five people were taken into custody as protests swelled Thursday night after ICE officers shot a man in northern Manhattan.
more: All were charged with obstructing governmental administration.
local.title: Several arrested in wake of ICE protest where Manhattan man was shot in the neck

local.b: Gothamist reports on Bronx homeowners facing foreclosure and looking for assistance.
local.title: Bronx homeowners facing foreclosure are in the market for assistance

local.h: Cornell students warned of fraternity abuse
local.b: Cornell's student government says it warned administrators about sexual assault and drugging in fraternities two years before the Jane Doe gang rape report.
local.title: Cornell students warned of fraternity 'rape culture' years before Jane Doe case

periods.name: Saturday
periods.text: Partly sunny, with a high near 68. North wind around 7 mph becoming southeast in the afternoon.

periods.name: Saturday Night
periods.text: Increasing clouds, with a low around 60. East wind 6 to 8 mph.

periods.name: Sunday
periods.text: Rain, mainly after 11am.  High near 67. East wind 10 to 15 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 80%. New precipitation amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible.

periods.name: Sunday Night
periods.text: Rain and possibly a thunderstorm before 2am, then a chance of rain and thunderstorms after 2am.  Low around 63. East wind 11 to 18 mph, with gusts as high as 29 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 90%. New rainfall amounts between a half and three quarters of an inch possible.

periods.name: Columbus Day
periods.text: A 30 percent chance of rain before 8am.  Cloudy through mid morning, then gradual clearing, with a high near 70.

periods.name: Monday Night
periods.text: Partly cloudy, with a low around 61.
